inference: N = 4 serves the most users (127,512) and N = 13 the fewest (30,324); the capacity ratio is 4.20x.
Capacity falls as N grows because each cell receives only 300/N channels: a smaller reuse cluster gives each cell more channels and therefore more Erlangs.
Capacity does NOT fall in proportion to the channel count: trunking efficiency improves with pool size (80.2 % at C = 75 versus 62.3 % at C = 23).
The price of a small N is co-channel interference (D/R = sqrt(3N) shrinks) - quantified by the integrated planner.
N = 13 leaves 1 channel unused (300 = 13 x 23 + 1) and 84 cells are not a whole number of 13-cell clusters; the textbook calculation assigns 23 channels to every cell and ignores this.
